title: Dependency Set
description: The complete set of dependency edges known for a contract at a boundary, partitioned into the direct edges and those reached only transitively. The set records its own completeness: bounded traversal is a normal and necessary implementation choice, but a truncated set that does not say it was truncated is indistinguishable from a complete one, which would let a consumer conclude that a dependency does not exist when the analysis merely stopped early.

id.description: Identifier for this set within the producing document.

edges.description: Every edge in the set. Rule dependency/transitive-dependency requires that each edge also appears in exactly one of direct or transitive, so the partition cannot silently lose an edge.

direct.description: Identifiers of the edges whose class is DIRECT. One hop from the analysed contract.

transitive.description: Identifiers of the edges reached only through one or more intermediate entities.

cycles.description: Cycles detected in this set, reported rather than resolved. A dependency graph can legitimately contain cycles, so removing them would hide a real topology; instead each cycle is reported with its path so a consumer can decide how to treat it.

edges.description: The edge identifiers forming the cycle, in traversal order.

length.description: The number of edges in the cycle.

maxDepth.description: The traversal depth the analysis was bounded by. Recorded so that a consumer can tell 'no deeper dependencies exist' from 'the search stopped here'.

truncated.description: Whether traversal stopped before exhausting the graph. When true, the set makes no claim of completeness, and a consumer must not report an absent dependency as a lack of dependency.

truncationReason.description: Why traversal stopped, when truncated. Required by rule dependency/transitive-dependency whenever truncated is true, so that a bound is always attributable to a stated limit rather than to an arbitrary cutoff.

unresolved.description: Dependencies that were identified but could not be resolved. Kept separate from edges because a resolver failure and an absent dependency are different findings that must not be merged.

reason.description: Why the dependency could not be resolved. A network failure is recorded here rather than being converted into an empty result.

boundary.description: The observation boundary the set was assembled at.
